tier: Pay as you go, Linux x86

free_tier.stated: Pay as you go includes $12 in credit each month per organization, renewing monthly, which covers 3,000 minutes on a 2-vCPU Linux x86 runner; there are no monthly subscription or per-seat fees. Sandboxes use the same compute rates as runners and are billed for reserved time.
free_tier.notes: The $12 monthly credit is the free allowance. The 2-vCPU/8 GB Linux x86 rate is $0.004 a minute, equal to $0.24 an hour; the operator's list gives Avrea Sandboxes at $0.24 an hour billed per second, while the pricing page says sandboxes are billed for reserved time and the blog says per-second billing.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine, not an object. A persistent disk add-on is priced at $0.50 per GB-month and 25 GB of cache storage per repository is included.

retention.stated: A paused sandbox is deleted with its disk 7 days after its time limit ended. Sandboxes that cannot pause, such as Windows, macOS and Linux arm64, are deleted with their disk at the limit; agent sandboxes boot once and their disk is not kept.

egress.terms: Networking is included in the price without separate bandwidth metering: 'Networking is included in the price, without separate bandwidth metering.' Git Mirroring outbound clone/fetch is $0.15 per GB, a separate add-on, and a static IP is $100 per IP per month.

interface_detail: Sandboxes are created in the console or with the Avrea CLI (avr vm create, avr vm ssh); an SSH terminal, RDP or VNC, scp/rsync via SSH config, and published HTTPS URLs are supported.
tooling: the Avrea console and the avr CLI; SSH, scp and rsync through a generated SSH config; published HTTPS URLs for previews; no rclone backend is documented.
chaining: A sandbox can start from a connected repository with package caches, pause and fork an eligible Linux x86 VM for parallel experiments, and publish a port over HTTPS for an agent preview.

limits.value: $12 of credit each month per organization, covering 3,000 minutes on a 2-vCPU Linux x86 runner
without a payment method a sandbox runs at most 2 hours from creation, extensions included; with one, the default is 8 hours and the maximum is 7 days
a paused sandbox is deleted with its disk 7 days after its time limit ended
an organization can keep one paused sandbox per vCPU of its sandbox quota

limits_note: macOS sandboxes require an account-level request and have a 24-hour minimum reservation. Forking is limited to supported paused Linux amd64 sandboxes and agent sandboxes cannot be forked.
binding_note: Without a payment method, the 2-hour cap on a sandbox ends the session first, before the $12 monthly credit is spent; a paused sandbox is then deleted after 7 days.

identity_cost.detail: The console sign-in at console.avrea.com offers 'Continue with GitHub' and 'Sign in with single sign-on (SSO)', with no email/password sign-in field rendered. The app bundle renders an email input only after the SSO option is chosen, to look up a SAML provider for a company domain ('No single sign-on is configured for that email. Continue with GitHub above.'), so the gate is GitHub or company SSO, not email. No phone or document field is shown, and no card is asked for before the $12 monthly credit is used. The exact card gate inside the console is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Without a payment method a sandbox stops after at most 2 hours, extensions included. A paused sandbox is deleted with its disk 7 days after its time limit; Windows, macOS and Linux arm64 sandboxes are always deleted with their disk. Agent sandboxes are deleted at session end and uncommitted work is lost.
confidence_note: Prices, the $12 monthly credit, the 2-hour no-payment cap, retention and the sign-in buttons are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-11-25. The sign-in buttons were re-read through every available route and the app bundle, which shows the email input is for company SSO lookup only. The exact card gate inside the console and per-sandbox egress byte terms are unverified: behind a sign-up.
